shared_elements: carved stone monolith with anthropomorphic/pillar form
low-relief carving on a flat or slightly curved face
horizontal band of repeated pattern (belt-like / zigzag register) crossing the surface
circle or disc motif in relief
curving arm-and-hand-like elements bent toward the front
U- or V-shaped hooked motifs beneath the horizontal band
justification: Both are upright stone monoliths whose relief is organised into a comparable vertical scheme: a crowded upper zone with sinuous curving creatures and a disc, a horizontal patterned band across the middle, and hooked U/V-shaped motifs in the lower zone, all executed in the same shallow, rounded, low-relief manner on coarse pale stone. The decisive difference is content and legibility: B is dominated by explicit animals (quadrupeds, a bird in profile, reptiles) arranged as registers on a flat slab, whereas A is a rounded three-dimensional body with head, arms, necklace and belt and no recognisable fauna.
